🖥 Colombia vs. Portugal: Injuries, predicted lineups & how to watch

📌 Get ready for Colombia vs Portugal in the 2026 World Cup! Discover the predicted lineup, injury news, and how to watch this Group K decider.

Colombia and Portugal meet in a huge Group K showdown with first place on the line at Hard Rock Stadium. Colombia have taken maximum points from their opening two matches and need only a draw to stay top, while Portugal must win to leapfrog them into first. With Cristiano Ronaldo back among the goals and Colombia carrying real momentum, this World Cup match preview has all the ingredients of a high-level group-stage decider between two genuine contenders.
​
Portugal have one notable concern in defence, with Tomas Araujo considered a doubt after picking up an injury in the opening match against Congo DR. Otherwise, Roberto Martinez has a strong squad available and is expected to keep Cristiano Ronaldo through the middle after his brace against Uzbekistan. Bernardo Silva and Rafael Leao are pushing for places, but Joao Felix may have done enough to keep his starting role in attack.
​
Colombia’s main injury news centers on Luis Suarez, who was forced off against Congo DR with a shoulder issue. The expectation, though, is that he will be fit enough to lead the line. Nestor Lorenzo could keep faith with the same side that won the first two matches, with Luis Diaz, James Rodriguez, and Jefferson Lerma all set to remain key figures. There is also set to be another start in central defence for Davinson Sanchez.
​
Colombia sits on six points and is riding high after two convincing opening performances.
​
Portugal responded emphatically to their opening draw, and the rout of Uzbekistan underlined the attacking quality in Martinez’s side.
​
The key trend is simple: these teams have only met once before, and this will be their first competitive encounter.
​
Colombia’s position at the top of Group K is deserved — they’ve been compact, direct, and dangerous on the counter, with Díaz a constant menace and Muñoz adding goals from deep. The knowledge that a draw is enough gives Lorenzo flexibility in how he sets his team up, and the enormous Colombian support expected at Hard Rock Stadium — given the city’s large Colombian community — will only add to that advantage.
​
Portugal, however, are no pushover. The 5-0 win over Uzbekistan showed what this side can do when the handbrake is off, and Ronaldo’s brace silenced those questioning his place in the eleven. The midfield trio of Fernandes, Neves, and Vitinha is among the most technically gifted at the tournament, and Lerma will have to be at his very best to contain them. Expect a tight, tactical contest — Colombia to hold their nerve and claim a draw, finishing top of the group.

Euro Digital: Europe is preparing money that will work even without the internet

Euro digital has taken a new step forward in Brussels.

The idea is for any citizen to be able to pay with a digital version of the euro, issued by the European Central Bank (ECB), including without an internet connection.

Payments can be made with a phone, card, online, and offline - and rely less on Visa, Mastercard, and private banks.

### What is already raising questions:
- Limits will be set on how much digital euros can be stored.
- Many stores may be required to accept it.
- Banks fear that some of the money will be taken from their accounts.
- Millions of citizens are concerned about privacy of data.

The ECB promises that digital euro will not replace cash, and offline payments will have an increased level of confidentiality (similar to cash).

However, the discussion in Europe has long gone beyond just the technology.

This is a question of power: do we need public digital money or are we opening the door to too much control over how we pay?

📌 Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs): Portable IDs for Web3

Main Points
⏺ DIDs are identifiers you control, not usernames owned by platforms
⏺ They can link to verifiable credentials like diplomas or KYC checks
⏺ This post explains how DIDs help build portable identity across apps

1️⃣ What Is a DID — a standardized identifier tied to keys you own, not to an email, phone number, or single company.
2️⃣ Verifiable Credentials — organizations can sign claims about you (for example, “passed KYC”, “finished course”) that you can present elsewhere.
3️⃣ User Control — you decide when and where to share proofs instead of giving every app full personal data.
4️⃣ Interoperability — multiple dApps, wallets, and even Web2 services can recognize the same DID as “you”.
5️⃣ Privacy Angle — combined with zero-knowledge proofs, DIDs can prove facts (age, residency, reputation) without revealing raw documents.

Final Thoughts

Decentralized identifiers turn identity from siloed accounts into something you own and reuse — a core building block for Web3 logins and reputation.

Former Ethereum Foundation developer Trent Van Epps warns that Ethereum could face a funding crisis within the next 3–9 months 

For years, the Ethereum Foundation has followed a “subtraction” strategy—gradually reducing its influence so the network can thrive independently. However, EF still remains a key pillar of legitimacy through its brand, ties to Vitalik Buterin, developer events, and ecosystem coordination.

The bigger issue is funding. After spending much of its ETH reserves on ecosystem growth, EF plans to cut annual spending from 15% to 5% by 2030. Meanwhile, its 4-year Client Incentive Program ended in April 2026 with no replacement announced.

Maintaining client teams, research, and protocol coordination costs around $30M per year. Without a sustainable funding model, Ethereum risks losing experienced developers and slowing progress on scaling, quantum-resistance research, and core network maintenance.

Ethereum’s biggest challenge may not be technology—it may be funding the people building it.

📈 Triangle pattern: basics and usage

A triangle is a chart pattern formed when highs and lows move toward each other, creating a narrowing range. It reflects market uncertainty — consolidation.

📶 Highs & lows: price moves inside a tightening range, converging to a point.
📐 Structure: over time, the chart forms a triangle with rising or falling boundaries.

How to use it? 🤔

🔘 Interaction: when price reaches the edges, traders expect a breakout.
🔘 Breakout: a move beyond the boundary can signal the start of a new trend.

❗️ Why it matters:
This pattern helps identify when the market may leave consolidation and start a strong move.
